qy_group_matrix_save_partial_list_only: Half applied: the selectable list was written, the ratios were not — newly granted pairs are billing at the fallback ratio
qy_group_matrix_mode_enforce_desc: Model groups outside the list cannot be selected by keys and requests get a 403. This is the only switch that cuts a batch of users off immediately.
qy_group_matrix_mode_switch_confirm: Before switching to enforce you must run a complete impact preview for this one user group; switching is also blocked when that preview was truncated.
qy_group_matrix_enforce_needs_saved_draf: There are unsaved cells on the matrix. Enforcing uses the list as stored in the database, so save or discard the draft first, then preview, then switch.
qy_group_matrix_enforce_preview_summary: This switch newly breaks {{broken}} pairs, covering {{tokens}} keys.
qy_group_matrix_allow_auto_desc: auto is not a real model group, so it never appears in the list; this switch alone controls whether it is injected back into the selectable range. Turning it off also stops keys from being saved as auto — the read and write sides share one rule. On first take-over it is pre-filled from the state before the change, so an in-use feature is never switched off by accident.
qy_group_matrix_empty_list_warning: {{userGroup}} is taken over but has no model group selected. This is a valid configuration (an isolation tier looks exactly like this), but after switching to enforce nobody in this tier will be able to select anything.
qy_group_matrix_note_placeholder: Why this group is taken over (recorded in the audit log)
qy_group_matrix_self_edge_hint: Removing a user group from its own list does NOT stop that tier from making requests: keys with an empty group bypass the whole check and route using the owner's user group directly. Clearing the diagonal only affects whether a key can be explicitly pinned to that group.
qy_group_matrix_preview_desc: Every number below is computed from the unsaved draft; this preview writes nothing.
qy_group_matrix_preview_already_broken: Already broken before this change (historical debt, unrelated)
qy_group_matrix_preview_traffic_7d: {{count}} real requests in the last {{days}} days
qy_group_matrix_preview_samples_truncate: Samples truncated; only the first few are shown.
qy_group_matrix_preview_truncated: The statistics are incomplete (timed out, or too many pairs). Switching to enforce is blocked in this state: better unable to switch than switching blind.
qy_group_matrix_preview_approximate_user: Traffic attribution is approximate: the log records the model group used at the time, while the user group is its current value, so users who changed tiers in between land in the wrong bucket.
qy_group_matrix_preview_empty_group_toke: A further {{count}} keys have no group set. They are structurally immune to this change: their requests skip the whole selectability check and route using the owner's user group.
qy_group_matrix_preview_auto_groups_shri: {{count}} keys have a dead group in their auto candidate list, so that list is silently shortened. This failure mode gives no other signal: requests still succeed, that group just never gets its turn.
qy_group_matrix_conflict_self_excluded: Some user groups are missing from their own list
qy_group_matrix_conflict_case_near_miss: Group names that differ only by letter case
qy_group_matrix_warn_group_missing: Group names absent from the group ratio table (currently billing at the 1.0 fallback)
qy_group_matrix_server_warnings: Things worth a look before saving (they do not block the save)
qy_group_matrix_shadow_denies_title: Key writes that shadow mode would have blocked
qy_group_matrix_snapshot_unloaded: The authoritative list has not loaded; none of it is in effect
qy_group_matrix_snapshot_unloaded_desc: The whole site is still admitting requests via the upstream global allowlist even though this table looks fully configured. Until the snapshot loads successfully, nothing configured here affects production.
qy_group_matrix_snapshot_stale: The authoritative list is stale but still in use
qy_group_matrix_snapshot_stale_desc: The last successful load was {{age}} ago. A stale snapshot is deliberately kept rather than discarded: discarding it would fall back to the looser upstream allowlist, and with zero-ratio model groups on this site that amounts to a revenue leak. The cost is that a recent revoke may not have reached this node yet.
qy_group_matrix_ratio_drift_banner: The group ratios were changed on the System Settings → Billing & Payment → Model groups page
qy_group_matrix_orphan_desc: A count of historical debt: {{tokens}} broken keys across {{users}} affected users. These are already in the "saves fine, fails on first request" state today.
qy_group_matrix_orphan_scope_note: ⚠ This report is computed against each owner's current selectable list, and the following user groups are already enforcing: {{groups}}. Keys broken by that switch also show up here, so these numbers are not a frozen pre-switch baseline.
qy_group_matrix_orphan_tokens: Keys whose group is not in their owner's selectable list
qy_group_matrix_orphan_deprecated: Keys whose group was deleted from the group ratio table
qy_group_matrix_orphan_auto_groups: Keys whose auto candidates include dead groups
qy_group_matrix_orphan_users_alert: Users whose user group is absent from the group ratio table (their requests bill at the 1.0 fallback)
qy_group_matrix_orphan_repair_confirm: Clear the group on key "{{token}}"? Afterwards its effective group always equals the owner's user group, so it works again immediately without changing what that user can reach. This is the only repair that is both safe and free of guesswork about the user's intent. The action is recorded in the audit log.
qy_group_matrix_orphan_repaired: The key's group has been cleared
qy_cfg_health_group_ratio_users: {{users}} users belong to groups missing from the group-ratio table; their requests are being billed at 1.0x silently (groups: {{groups}}). Check under System Settings → Billing & Payment → Model groups whether these names were deleted or mistyped.
qy_cfg_health_group_ratio_observed: The extension has actually hit these groups missing from the group-ratio table: {{groups}}. Upstream fails open and bills at 1.0x.
qy_cfg_usd_rate_title: Amounts on this page are in USD
qy_cfg_usd_rate_desc: Current rate: 1 USD = {{rate}} quota. Only the unit shown changes — what is saved and written to the audit log is still the quota integer. If the site rate is changed later, every threshold saved here keeps the same stored integer but stands for a different amount of money.
qy_cfg_usd_unavailable_title: USD entry is unavailable at the current rate
qy_cfg_usd_unavailable_desc: The site is set to 1 USD = {{rate}} quota, which cannot express every quota value in USD without rounding. Rather than show a rounded amount you might save by accident, the amount fields below fall back to raw quota units.
qy_cfg_usd_unavailable_no_rate: The site has no usable USD rate configured, so the amount fields below fall back to raw quota units. Set the quota-per-unit rate in System Settings to a whole number that divides 1,000,000 (the default 500,000 does) to enter amounts in USD.
qy_cfg_usd_step_hint: Smallest step is {{step}} (1 quota); amounts that do not land on a whole quota are rejected.
qy_chops_disable_desc: Manually disable {{count}} selected channel(s). They leave routing immediately and can be re-enabled at any time.
qy_chops_reset_desc: Clears statistics on {{count}} selected channel(s). Cleared values cannot be restored.
qy_chops_reset_already_zero: {{count}} of them already have a used quota of 0 and will not change.
qy_chops_reset_used_quota_not_selected: "Clear used quota" is not checked, so the amount above will not be cleared.
qy_chops_reset_desc_one: Clears the statistics of channel "{{name}}". Cleared values cannot be restored.
qy_chops_reset_scope_hint: This clears "Used" (this site's cumulative spend for the channel), not "Remaining" (the upstream account balance). Real upstream usage is untouched.
qy_chops_reset_pick_desc: Pick the channels to clear — no need to turn on Batch mode. This clears the "Used" half only; "Remaining" is untouched.
qy_chops_reset_pick_empty: No channels on this page can be cleared.
qy_chops_reset_irreversible_desc: Once confirmed, the used quota this site has accumulated for these channels is wiped and cannot be restored. No account balance is involved, and real upstream usage is untouched.
qy_chops_reset_used_quota_hint: This site's cumulative spend for the channel, shown in the Used column. Cannot be undone; usage logs are unaffected.
qy_chops_reset_balance_hint: A cached display value only. Just a few channel types can fetch it, and the next balance refresh overwrites it. Usually only needed after switching upstream accounts.
qy_chops_delete_desc: Deletes the following {{count}} channel(s) and their model routing entries. This cannot be undone.
qy_chops_no_permission: No permission to perform this action
qy_chops_result_desc: Per-channel outcome. Only channels needing attention are listed.
qy_chops_item_not_found: Channel not found; it may have been deleted by another admin
qy_chops_item_db_error: Database operation failed; check the server log
qy_chops_item_aborted: Request interrupted; this channel was not processed
qy_chops_item_no_change: Already in the target state; nothing to change
qy_chops_item_not_applied: Status was not applied: this node's cache disagrees with the database (common in multi-node deployments). The channel is unchanged — retry after a cache sync interval; retrying has no side effects.
qy_chops_toast_reset_ok: {{count}} channel(s) cleared, wiping {{amount}} of used quota
qy_err_chops_no_ids: Select at least one channel first
qy_err_chops_too_many: At most 200 channels per batch; please split the operation
qy_err_chops_bad_status: Only enable and manual-disable are allowed in batch
qy_err_chops_nothing_to_reset: Select at least one item to reset
qy_group_matrix_axis_row_hint: Each row is a tier of people: which user group an account belongs to, assigned by an admin. Editing a row changes what everyone in that tier can select.
qy_group_matrix_axis_col_hint: Each column is a set of channels: which upstream channels a request is finally routed to, driven by the channel's group field. It is not a set of users.
qy_group_matrix_axis_same_name_note: Both axes share one underlying name list, so the same name can appear on both. Identical names are not the same thing: a row is a tier of users, a column is a set of channels.
qy_group_matrix_axis_create_hint: Groups cannot be created here. A model group is a new row on the Model groups page; a user group is created with the "New user group" button above the table on the User groups page:
qy_group_matrix_axis_create_link: System Settings → Billing & Payment → User groups / Model groups
qy_group_matrix_axis_create_empty: No user groups here yet. Create one under System Settings → Billing & Payment → User groups with the "New user group" button above the table, then come back here to grant it model groups.
qy_group_matrix_axis_create_empty_no_acc: No user groups here yet. Creating one means using the "New user group" button under System Settings → Billing & Payment → User groups, and that page is open to super admins only — ask a super admin to create the group, then come back here to grant it model groups.
qy_group_matrix_axis_create_need_super: That step needs a super admin: System Settings → Billing & Payment → User groups is open to super admins only. Ask a super admin to create the group, then come back here to grant it model groups.
qy_plan_holders_desc: {{plan}} · {{total}} user(s) currently on this plan. Multiple subscriptions held by the same person still take only one seat.
qy_plan_holders_empty: Nobody is on this plan right now
qy_plan_holders_empty_desc: Expired and cancelled subscriptions do not take a seat, so they are not listed here.
qy_plan_holders_col_subs_hint: How many active subscriptions this user holds on this plan; multiple ones still take only a single seat.
qy_plan_holders_user_deleted_hint: This user has been deleted but the subscription still takes a seat — the account no longer shows up in user management.
qy_plan_holders_open: View the {{n}} user(s) on this plan
qy_group_scope_matrix_desc: Rows are user groups (which tier a person belongs to); columns are model groups (which pool of channels a request is routed to); each cell holds that pair's ratio. While a user group has no usable list of its own, what it may use is decided by each model group's "User selectable" switch on the Model groups page, and this page does not restrict it. Once a usable list is set, only the groups on that list are allowed.
qy_group_pricing_moved_desc: The two JSON editors this page used to carry — "Inter-group overrides" (special ratio rules) and "Special usable group rules" — are gone from here. Inter-group overrides moved to the User groups page: click Edit on a tier and set a ratio per model group in the dialog; leave one blank and it falls back to that model group's base ratio. The special usable group rules (+: / -: differences) were retired entirely: they never actually took effect — upstream unconditionally re-added the user group to its own list after applying the differences, which cancelled out the only half that mattered (hiding a group from its own tier). There is now exactly one answer to "which tier can pick which model groups": tick the usable list in that tier's edit dialog on the User groups page, and once ticked only those are allowed; a tier with no list follows each model group's own "User selectable" switch. Billing behaviour in the backend is unchanged. What stays on this page (Model groups) is the model-group side: group name, base ratio, user selectable, group note, plus the auto order and the per-token custom group limit. Top-up ratios belong to the User groups page.
qy_group_scope_state_empty_hint: "{{userGroup}}" has a scope but not a single model group selected. Under enforce mode, tokens from this tier that name a model group explicitly get a 403; tokens with an empty group skip this check entirely and keep billing at the user group's own ratio — an empty scope does not stop those.
qy_group_scope_unset_hint: No scope set: this tier is not restricted by this page. Which model groups it may use comes from the global "user selectable groups" setting (including its +: / -: rules), each billed at that model group's fallback ratio. To restrict it here, set a scope for this user group first.
qy_group_scope_unscoped_note: {{count}} user group(s) still have no scope ({{groups}}) — they are not restricted by this page; what they may use comes from the global "user selectable groups" setting, each at the fallback ratios. Newly created user groups start out this way too.
qy_group_scope_all_scoped_note: Every user group has a scope set. A user group created elsewhere starts with no scope, and is then not restricted by this page — what it may use comes from the global "user selectable groups" setting.
qy_group_scope_edit_desc: Choose which model groups this tier may use, and how strictly the scope is applied.
qy_group_scope_dialog_desc: Select the model groups this tier may use and override their ratios. Changes that revoke access or reprice can only be saved after the impact preview has been seen.
qy_group_scope_dialog_gone_desc: Another administrator may have just removed it on the Model groups page. Close this window and reload the list.
qy_group_scope_switch_label: Set a scope for this user group
qy_group_scope_switch_on_desc: Scope is set: only the model groups selected below are usable. The global "user selectable groups" list and its +: / -: rules no longer apply to this tier.
qy_group_scope_switch_off_desc: No scope set: this tier is not restricted by this page and falls back to the global "user selectable groups" list. Turning this switch off does not restrict them — it hands the decision back to the global setting.
qy_group_scope_empty_warning: The scope for "{{userGroup}}" is currently empty: no model group is usable. This is a valid configuration (an isolation or ban tier). Note that enforce mode only stops tokens that name a model group explicitly — tokens with an empty group skip this check and keep working.
qy_group_scope_empty_todo_title: Some user groups have a scope but no model group selected
qy_group_scope_empty_todo_desc: Users in these tiers cannot point a token at any model group right now (enforce mode returns 403 for such requests; tokens with an empty group are unaffected). Select the model groups they may use, or confirm that granting none is intended.
qy_group_scope_enforce_plan_bypass_note: Enforce mode does not override plan unlocks: a user in this tier who holds a plan that unlocks a model group can still point a token at it (unlocks are a union applied after the scope). To close that path too, change the plan_entitlement switch or that plan's unlock bindings.
qy_group_ratio_inherit_vs_zero_hint: Leave empty to inherit this model group's fallback ratio; type 0 to make it explicitly free. The two differ by the full charge — do not confuse them.
qy_group_matrix_reachable_via_plan: Reachable via plan: {{plans}}. This cell is outside the user group's scope, yet users holding these plans can still use it.
qy_plan_entitlement_title: Model group unlocks & balance scope for "{{plan}}"
qy_plan_entitlement_desc: Unlocks are not tied to any user group: whoever buys this plan gets these model groups regardless of the tier they are in. Ratios are not configured here — they are always determined by the (user group, model group) pair.
qy_plan_entitlement_impact: {{count}} active subscription(s) currently hold this plan — changes take effect for them immediately.
qy_plan_entitlement_disabled_alert: Plan unlocks are currently switched off — nothing configured here takes effect
qy_plan_entitlement_disabled_hint: plan_entitlement.enabled is off: subscribers do not receive the model groups this plan unlocks, and the balance scope is not enforced. This page still saves (the change is stored and takes effect the moment the switch is turned back on), but until then it has no effect on users.
qy_plan_section_unlock_title: Unlocked model groups (what this plan actually sells)
qy_plan_section_unlock_desc: This is an add-on subscription: buyers keep their user group and gain the model groups below on top of it — they are never moved to a different user group. Ratios are not configured here; they are always determined by the (user group, model group) pair, and the plan carries none of them.
qy_plan_section_quota_desc: This quota is the plan's own pool, separate from the user's wallet balance. Four things below decide how it is spent: how much there is, how often it refills, which model groups it may be spent on, and what happens once it runs out.
qy_plan_wallet_overflow_on_hint: On: once the plan quota runs out the request keeps going and is charged to the user's wallet balance, still at the (user group, model group) ratio.
qy_plan_wallet_overflow_off_hint: Off: once the plan quota runs out, a model group that only this plan grants (the user's own user group does not contain it) is rejected outright with "insufficient subscription quota" and may not fall back to the wallet balance — access to such a group was bought with the plan, so it ends when the quota does.
qy_plan_unlock_groups_empty: No model groups available — create them under System Settings → Billing & Payment → Model groups first.
qy_plan_unlock_groups_hint: Candidates come only from the model group axis (the keys of the group ratio table). Selecting none is valid: the plan then sells quota without unlocking anything. Struck-through entries are bindings whose model group no longer exists in the ratio table — they already have no effect; unselect them to clear them out.
qy_plan_balance_scope_label: Where this plan's balance can be spent
qy_plan_balance_scope_universal_desc: The balance can also be spent on other model groups. This is the existing behaviour; upgrading changes nothing.
qy_plan_balance_scope_restricted_hint: The balance can only be spent on the model groups bound above. Requests on any other model group skip this plan (this is not "insufficient balance" — the balance is still there, it just cannot be used) and fall back to the wallet; a skipped plan also cannot block that wallet fallback.
qy_plan_balance_scope_need_binding: "Restricted" requires at least one bound model group that still exists — otherwise no request can ever use the balance: users see it, cannot spend it, and it expires worthless.
qy_plan_balance_scope_not_enforced: "Restricted" is not in effect on the billing path yet
qy_plan_balance_scope_not_enforced_hint: Balance-scope filtering is not wired into billing yet: this setting is saved but does not limit spending — the balance can still be spent on any model group. Until the wiring is complete, do not price or reconcile as if the restriction were active.
qy_plan_bound_group_missing_alert: These bound model groups no longer exist in the group ratio table
qy_plan_ratio_table_title: What will actually be charged (computed live)
qy_ent_failed: Could not be loaded — refresh to retry
qy_ent_scope_universal: Universal — usable on any model group
qy_ent_scope_restricted: Restricted — only the model groups unlocked above
qy_ent_scope_restricted_off: Restricted (not enforced yet — the balance can still be spent on any model group)
qy_ent_summary_title: Model groups unlocked by your plans:
qy_ent_summary_none: Your plans unlock no additional model groups
qy_ent_summary_failed: Plan entitlements could not be loaded — which model groups your plans unlock, and what their balance can be spent on, cannot be shown right now. Refresh to retry.
qy_ent_restricted_notice: One of your plans has a balance restricted to specific model groups: requests on any other group will not consume it and will be charged to your wallet balance instead.
qy_ent_restricted_off: One of your plans is marked Restricted, but that restriction is not enforced on the billing path yet — its balance can still be spent on any model group.
qy_ent_wallet_blocked: One of your plans does not allow falling back to your wallet balance once its own quota runs out — this only affects the model groups that plan unlocks for you; groups your own user group already contains can still be paid from your wallet.
qy_billing_order_fixed: The billing order is fixed and needs no setup: every request looks at your plans first — if an active plan covers the model group of this request within its balance scope and still holds enough balance for this call, the plan is charged; otherwise your wallet balance is.
qy_gs_two_roles_desc: The same name can appear in two places: on a person it is a user group (assigned by admins; it decides the top-up discount and which model groups they may pick), on a token it is a model group (it decides which channels the request is routed to and which base ratio is charged). One string namespace underneath, two completely different jobs.
qy_gs_where_base_ratio: Model group base ratios, auto order, and the per-token custom group limit live on the Model groups page.
qy_gs_where_topup: Top-up discount ratios and the auto-by-default switch live on the User groups page.
qy_gs_where_cross_ratio: The user group x model group override ratio and the usable model groups live behind Edit on that row of the User groups page - set them per model group in the dialog.
qy_gs_where_usable_list: "User selectable" is a switch column on the Model groups page - it decides whether a model group can be picked by user groups that have no usable list of their own.
qy_gs_json_escape_desc: Edit this page's options as raw JSON. This edits the current draft: Apply reads it back into the table above, and you still have to press Save on the page for it to reach the server.
qy_gs_json_invalid: Invalid JSON: {{keys}}. Apply stays disabled until it parses - feeding broken JSON back into the table would empty it, which looks exactly like a site that was never configured.
qy_gs_user_groups_desc: A user group decides which tier a person belongs to: the top-up discount and which model groups they may pick. It does not decide which channels a request is routed to - that is what a model group does.
qy_gs_user_groups_empty: No user group has been observed yet.
qy_gs_user_groups_no_roster: The user group list cannot be loaded (extension disabled or backend unreachable), so the table below is empty right now - that does not mean the site has no user groups, only that they cannot be read. Until this recovers, creating, editing (note, top-up ratio, usable model groups) and deleting are all unavailable on this page. Check the extension and backend first.
qy_gs_topup_hint: Top-up ratios are per user group: leave it empty to charge full price (same as 1). It must be greater than 0 - on the top-up side 0 does not mean free, payment falls back to 1. Creating, renaming and deleting all happen on this table: create with the button above it, rename and delete from each row's Edit dialog.
qy_gs_cross_ratio_label: User group x model group override ratios
qy_gs_fallback_usable_desc: The global selectable-groups list. User groups that have no scope of their own fall back to this list; groups with a scope ignore it and use the cells ticked in the matrix instead.
qy_gs_fallback_usable_empty: The global list is empty - user groups without a scope can therefore only pick the model group that shares their own name.
qy_gs_model_groups_desc: A model group decides which channels a request is routed to and which base ratio is charged. It has nothing to do with which tier a person belongs to - that is what a user group does.
qy_gs_model_table_desc: One row per model group. The base ratio is options.GroupRatio, which the three billing paths multiply directly.
qy_gs_delete_row_hint: Deleting a row in this table only removes its base ratio; the group name itself, its grants, plan unlocks, auto order entry and token bindings all stay. To actually delete a model group, use the delete action in the registry table below — it computes the impact first and then cascades. Usable scope is edited here:
qy_gs_invalid_ratio_warn: These rows have a ratio that does not parse: {{names}}. Saving is disabled - an empty box would be written as 0 (the whole model group becomes free), so a number has to be typed explicitly.
qy_gs_missing_ratio_title: Model groups without a base ratio
qy_gs_missing_ratio_warn: {{names}} appear in the global selectable list but not in the ratio table. Users can pick them, and billing silently falls back to 1.0 when no ratio is found - a 1.0 nobody configured.
qy_gs_no_channels_title: Model groups with no usable channel
qy_gs_no_channels_warn: {{names}} have a ratio but not a single enabled channel underneath. They look identical to a healthy group in the token dropdown, and every request that picks one returns 503.
qy_gs_free_ratio_warn: Model groups with a base ratio of 0: {{names}}. Calls billed as these groups are entirely free - confirm that this is intended.
qy_plan_wallet_overflow_off_membership: This switch has no say over model groups the user's own user group already contains: those requests do not need this plan at all, so the wallet balance can always pay for them. It is therefore not a way to say "this user may not spend their wallet" — no setting on this site expresses that.
qy_plan_entitlement_pending_pay_blocked: Loading the model groups this plan unlocks and where its balance may be spent. These are terms you need before paying, so payment stays disabled until they load.
qy_lot_ball_tier_split_even: Split evenly among all winners of this tier
qy_lot_ball_split_note: This column is the prize form, not what you receive. The "tier budget" of a floating prize is split evenly among all winners of that tier — the more winners, the smaller each share. "Budget shares" on a fixed prize works the same way: once winners outnumber the shares, the shares x amount budget is split evenly too. The odds are always exactly what the number pool's combinatorics says; it is the amount that floats.
qy_lot_v_ball_pool_short: The series pool does not cover this round: total fixed-prize budget + pool x total floating share must not exceed the pool. A draft like this is refused at publish time and stays a draft forever. Fund the series first, or lower the tiers.
qy_lot_v_ball_pool_share_short: A floating tier's budget, computed from the series pool as it stands, is smaller than the maximum number of entries: on oversubscription some winners would be diluted to zero, and publishing is refused. Raise that tier's share, fund the series, or lower the entry cap.
qy_gs_auto_list_empty_warn: The auto order is currently empty while this switch is on - a newly registered user's first token lands on the auto group with no candidate model group at all, and its very first call fails. Set the auto order on the Model groups page first, or turn this switch off.
qy_mg_registry_desc: One row per model group name. This answers the three things the ratio table above cannot: where the name came from, which description users actually see, and how to really delete it (with an impact preview and a cascading cleanup).
qy_mg_registry_empty: No model groups registered yet. Registration is backfilled automatically (from the group ratio table plus abilities); check back shortly.
qy_mg_note_placeholder: Leave empty to fall back to the global selectable-list description
qy_mg_note_saved: Note saved; it takes effect for users immediately
qy_mg_note_overrides_usable: This note is what users see now; the global selectable-list text “{{text}}” is overridden and hidden.
qy_mg_note_falls_back: The note is empty, so users see the global selectable-list text: “{{text}}”.
qy_mg_deleted: Deleted, and these options were cleaned up: {{keys}}
qy_mg_delete_desc: Deleting also clears every reference in the group ratio table, the global “user selectable groups” list, the auto order, inter-group ratios, user-group grants and plan unlocks. Channels and tokens are left untouched — the two checkboxes below explain why.
qy_mg_delete_blocked_title: Cannot delete: something must be handled by you first
qy_mg_impact_pinned: User groups pinning it as their default
qy_mg_impact_cross_ratio: User groups with an inter-group ratio for it
qy_mg_impact_residues: Residues per module (zero-row entries are listed too: “nothing here” and “not checked” are different)
qy_mg_force_has_route: I understand {{channels}} enabled channels / {{abilities}} ability rows still bind this group. Deleting the name does not touch those channels, so they become “has channels but nobody can select it”; and once the name leaves the ratio table, any request that still reaches it is billed silently at the fail-open 1.0 ratio.
qy_mg_force_orphan_tokens: I understand {{tokens}} enabled tokens (owned by {{owners}} users) point at this group and every request from them will be rejected afterwards. This action will not rewrite those tokens — that would change a billing group on the user's behalf.
qy_ugr_registry_desc: Each row is one tier of users. The table above is observed from users.group; this one is maintained by you — create, rename and migrate-then-delete live here, because a freshly created group with nobody in it exists only in the registry.
qy_ugr_registry_empty: No user group registered yet. Backfill picks them up from the current users.group values, or create one directly.
qy_ugr_create_desc: This writes one registry row only. Its usable model groups and ratios are configured in the user-group × model-group matrix; the top-up discount is in the table above.
qy_ugr_field_name: Group name (billing and auth match it exactly)
qy_ugr_field_display_name: Display name (falls back to the group name)
qy_ugr_field_note_placeholder: Who is this tier for, and why it exists
qy_ugr_create_empty_warn: A brand-new group can select no model group at all and has no channel pool of its own: once you move users in, their tokens get 403 (no grant) or 503 (empty-group tokens resolve to nothing). Grant it access and pin a default model group before moving anyone.
qy_ugr_created: User group “{{name}}” created (0 users, 0 tokens — it affects no request yet)
qy_ugr_rename_desc: Configuration follows the name: cross ratios, top-up discount, scope and grants, transfer rules, plan upgrade/downgrade groups and sold-subscription snapshots are all rewritten.
qy_ugr_rename_carries: This tier currently holds {{users}} users; their users.group is rewritten inside a single main-database transaction. If the count changed after you opened this dialog the save is rejected and you are asked to reload — that is not a failure, it stops you from deciding on a stale number.
qy_ugr_delete_desc: Deleting is both a bulk repricing and a bulk permission change. When the group still holds users you must pick a migration target — deleting outright points those accounts at a group that does not exist, and group ratio resolution is fail-open at 1.0, so they would be billed silently at full price.
qy_ugr_delete_blocked_title: Cannot delete: something must be handled by you first
qy_ugr_migrate_to_hint: Migration and deletion happen in one operation: users.group and the subscription snapshots are rewritten inside a single main-database transaction first, then the extension-database config and the options keys are cleared. At every interruption point the group name a user points at still has complete configuration.
qy_ugr_diff_unchanged: Usable model groups and ratios are unchanged ({{count}} groups)
qy_ugr_diff_removed: Lost (tokens on these pools start failing with 403):
qy_ugr_diff_loses_everything: Migration target “{{target}}” can select no model group at all — every token of these {{users}} users starts failing the moment the migration lands.
qy_ugr_ack_loses_everything: I understand that after migrating to “{{target}}” all tokens of these {{users}} users stop working immediately, and I intend that.
qy_ugr_gate_needs_target: This tier still holds users; pick a migration target before deleting.
qy_ugr_gate_blocked: The reason the Delete button is dead is in the red notice above - that has to be handled by you first.
qy_ugr_gate_needs_ack: The migration target cannot reach a single model group. Tick the confirmation box above to acknowledge that every token these users hold stops working the moment the migration completes.
qy_ugr_gate_loading: The impact report is still loading. User count, token count and the post-migration diff are not in yet; deleting is possible once it lands.
qy_ugr_gate_refreshing: The diff is being recomputed for the new migration target - what you see is still the previous target's. Deleting is possible once it lands.
qy_ugr_next_upstream_default: This tier can never be deleted or renamed, and no action unlocks it. If what you actually want is "stop new sign-ups from landing here", change the default tier for new registrations at the top of this page. If you want this tier to have different pricing or a different usable range, click Edit and change it in place - you do not need to delete it.
qy_ugr_next_blocking_plans: Go to the Plans page and repoint (or clear) the upgrade/downgrade group of every plan listed above onto another user group, then come back here to delete.
qy_ugr_next_blocking_residues: Every configuration listed above points at this tier, and only you know the correct new value. Repoint them onto another user group (or delete those rows) on the corresponding pages first, then come back - the list carries table names and row counts so you can check them off directly.
qy_ugr_next_no_migration_target: This is currently the only established user group on the site, so these users have nowhere to go. Create a target group with "New user group" on this page first, then come back to delete this one and migrate them.
qy_ugr_rename_blocked_title: Note: this tier cannot be renamed right now either
qy_ugr_impact_residues: Cascading cleanup (rows with 0 are listed too: “nothing here” and “not checked” must look different)
qy_ugr_deleted_migrated: User group “{{name}}” deleted; {{users}} users migrated to “{{target}}”
qy_ugr_stragglers: Done, but {{count}} users are still attached to the original group (concurrent writes during the operation). They are orphans right now and bill at the fail-open 1.0 ratio — move them to the target group by hand.
qy_ugr_migrate_title: Move everyone in “{{name}}” to another group
qy_ugr_migrate_desc: Moves people only, it does not delete the group. Their users.group is rewritten in a single main-database transaction and their own subscription downgrade snapshots follow; user caches are invalidated one by one right after, so the new usable list and ratios take effect immediately.
qy_ugr_migrate_keeps_source_title: This is not a deletion: “{{name}}” still exists afterwards
qy_ugr_migrate_keeps_source_desc: Migration only moves people. “{{name}}” itself — its note, top-up ratio, usable model groups and every per-cell ratio — is kept byte for byte; only the head count drops to 0. Plans that point at it (upgrade/downgrade group) and the “which group new sign-ups land in” setting are left untouched too, so if either still points here, people will trickle back in. To stop it from receiving users at all, change those two after the migration.
qy_ugr_migrate_empty_tokens_hint: {{count}} of them are group-less tokens (no token group set). Their model group is resolved from the user's group, so they are the ones whose behaviour changes most directly — the diff above applies to them item by item.
qy_ugr_migrate_no_target: There is no second registered user group on this site, so these people have nowhere to go. Create a target group with “New user group” above first.
qy_ugr_migrate_refill_title: People will still be placed into this group after the migration
qy_ugr_migrate_refill_plans: The upgrade/downgrade group of these plans still points at “{{name}}”: {{plans}}. Migration does not touch them (the group name still exists, so the plans keep working), which means the next buyer lands here again. To stop it from receiving users, repoint those references on the Plans page.
qy_ugr_migrate_refill_residues: The following settings still put new users into "{{name}}": {{sources}}. Migration does not touch them, so this tier starts filling up again from the next signup (or the next time they fire). Change those settings after the migration if you want it to stop receiving users.
qy_ugr_migrate_refill_toast: Migrated, but this group will be refilled: {{source}}. Change that source if you want it to stop receiving users.
qy_ugr_migrate_stragglers: Migration finished, but {{count}} users are still attached to the source group (concurrent sign-ups or group changes during the operation). The source group is fully configured, so they are not orphans and are not mispriced — click “Move users” once more to gather them up.
qy_ugr_migrated: Moved {{users}} users from “{{from}}” to “{{target}}”. The source group still exists (now with 0 users) and its configuration was not touched.
qy_ugr_migrate_gate_needs_target: Pick a target user group first.
qy_ugr_migrate_gate_needs_ack: The target group cannot use a single model group. Tick the confirmation box above to acknowledge that every token of these users stops working the moment the migration completes.
qy_ugr_migrate_gate_no_users: This group currently has no registered users, so there is nothing to move.
qy_ugr_migrate_no_users: No users in this group right now — nothing to move.
qy_tl_desc: The block above is the site-wide fallback. Here you can give one user group its own tier: only the items you tick are overridden, the rest keep following the site-wide values.
qy_tl_note_title: "Not overridden" and "overridden to 0" are different things
qy_tl_note_desc: Unticked = this item follows the site-wide threshold and changes with it. Ticked and set to 0 = this tier turns that gate off (no limit), and site-wide changes no longer affect it. The two point in opposite directions, which is why the UI uses a checkbox rather than an empty input to tell them apart.
qy_tl_empty: No tiers yet — every user is on the site-wide thresholds.
qy_tl_at_cap: Tier limit reached ({{max}}). Delete the ones you no longer need first.
qy_tl_form_desc: Tick only the items this tier should set on its own. Changes take effect immediately, apply to transfers started afterwards, and are written to the audit log together with your account.
qy_tl_deleted: Tier deleted — that group falls back to the site-wide thresholds
qy_tl_field_group_ph: Pick or type a user group name
qy_tl_field_group_desc: This is the **user group** (who the account is), not the model group (which channel pool a request goes to). The group name is this tier's primary key and cannot be renamed after saving — create a new tier and delete the old one instead.
qy_tl_group_picker_empty: No matching user group. Type a name to use it as-is.
qy_tl_field_enabled_desc: When off, the whole tier is inert and this group falls back to the site-wide thresholds. The effective values below still show what it would look like once enabled.
qy_tl_fallback_hint: Unticking returns this to the site-wide {{value}}.
qy_tl_row_invalid_desc: This tier combined with the current site-wide thresholds is self-contradictory (for example a per-transfer minimum above the per-transfer maximum), so the backend has suspended transfers for this group. Note this can happen without touching the tier — changing the site-wide values is enough. Fix either this tier or the site-wide block.
qy_tl_global_invalid_desc: Transfers are suspended entirely, and tiers do not take effect in that state. Fix the site-wide values in the card above first.
qy_tl_unknown_title: Some tiers point at user groups the site has not registered
qy_tl_unknown_desc: {{groups}}. This is a warning only: legacy groups (already gone from the registry but still on some users) are exactly the accounts most likely to need their own thresholds, so saving is not blocked. Please double-check for typos.
qy_tl_delete_desc: After deletion the "{{group}}" group falls back to the site-wide thresholds (usually looser). What this tier contained will only survive in the audit log.
qy_tl_err_empty_tier: Tick at least one item, otherwise this tier is identical to not configuring anything.
qy_mg_delete_no_registry: This model group has not been established yet, so there is nothing to delete. Right now it is only a name in the ratio table or the selectable switches - press Save at the top of the page to establish this row first, then come back to delete it.
qy_mg_note_legacy_active: Note is empty, so users currently see the legacy whitelist text: {{text}}
qy_mg_table_desc: Group name / base ratio / user selectable / group note. "User selectable" decides whether user groups without their own usable list can pick it; "group note" is the description users see when choosing a group while creating an API key (a user group can override it per cell).
qy_mg_usable_value_is_legacy: Read-only reference. The group names listed here are exactly the ones whose "User selectable" switch is on above; the text after each name is a legacy description, now edited in the "Group note" column instead.
qy_ug_backfilled: "{{name}}" previously existed only in the user table; a registry row has been created for it.
qy_ug_cell_note_placeholder: Note shown only to this user group; leave empty to use the model group's default note
qy_ug_delete_not_addressable: The delete endpoint cannot find this name: it has no registry row and nobody in the user table carries it (most likely just a stale key in the ratio table).
qy_ug_dialog_desc: Everything about this user group: note, top-up ratio, which model groups it can use, and a per-model-group ratio and note.
qy_ug_rename_needs_registry: Not established yet - press Save once.
qy_ug_delete_default_note: System default tier, cannot be deleted - open Delete for the reason and what to do instead.
qy_ug_rename_blocked_upstream_default: System default tier, cannot be renamed - fill in the display name above instead.
qy_ug_rename_blocked_title: This tier cannot be renamed right now
qy_ug_scope_follows_model_group: No list set · follows each model group's "User selectable"
qy_ug_table_hint: One row = one user group. Click Edit to set its note, top-up ratio, usable model groups, and a per-model-group ratio and note.
qy_ug_topup_hint_inline: Empty = no discount, charged at full price. Fill it in to charge that multiple: 0.9 = 10% off. It must be greater than 0 - on the top-up side 0 does not mean free, payment still charges full price.
qy_ug_topup_invalid: Top-up ratio accepts decimal numbers only (e.g. 0.9 or 0).
qy_ug_unregistered_hint: This user group is currently only a group name in the user table and has not been established yet. Pressing Save establishes it; after that the note, rename and delete all work.
qy_ug_topup_readonly_hint: Read-only reference. Top-up ratios are now saved one group at a time: click Edit on a row and change it in the dialog. Editing the whole JSON here would overwrite someone else's just-changed tier with the snapshot you loaded, so it is disabled.
qy_ug_open_advanced_matrix: Advanced: bulk column edits, cross-tier comparison and orphan token triage
qy_ug_cell_note_pending: Saved, but users cannot see it yet ({{state}}). What they see right now is: {{note}}
qy_ug_cell_note_pending_generic: not in effect under the current settings
qy_mg_note_needs_registry: This model group has not been established yet, so the note cannot be saved. Press Save at the top of the page to establish this row first, then come back and write the note.
qy_mg_delete_discards_draft: Heads up: this page has unsaved changes (base ratio or "User selectable"). Deleting reloads the whole table from the server and those changes will be reverted. To keep them, cancel, press Save at the top of the page, then delete.
qy_ugl_section_title: Model groups this tier can use ({{count}})
qy_ugl_own_note: This tier has a list of its own and it is already set to "enforce now": only the model groups below are usable, and the global "user selectable groups" setting (including its +: / -: rules) no longer applies to it. Emptying the list asks you a question first — "allow nothing" and "fall back to the global list" are opposites.
qy_ugl_fallback_note: This tier has no list of its own yet. What you see below is what it can **actually** use right now, decided by the global "user selectable groups" setting. Adding or removing anything here creates a list of its own for this tier (seeded from the current state, observing without blocking).
qy_ugl_empty_scope: This tier's list is empty — that is the opposite of having no list at all. Once you switch to "enforce now", tokens from this tier that name a model group explicitly get a 403; tokens with an empty group skip this check entirely and keep working, so an empty list does not stop those. To make it follow the global "user selectable groups" setting again, add any entry back with "Add model group" and then remove it — that is where the "fall back to the global list" exit lives.
qy_ugl_empty_fallback: The global "user selectable groups" setting currently grants this tier nothing. Use "Add model group" below to give it a list of its own.
qy_ugl_add_title: Pick from the model groups not assigned yet ({{count}}). The number in brackets is its base ratio — without a per-cell override that is what gets billed.
qy_ugl_add_none: Every model group on the site is already in this tier's list.
qy_ugl_origin_plan_hint: It is not in this tier's list, but users who bought "{{plans}}" can still use it (plan unlocks are a union applied after the list replacement). The ratio on this cell is still billing real money and can be edited here.
qy_ugl_create_title: Give "{{userGroup}}" a model group list of its own
qy_ugl_create_desc: Right now this tier follows the global "user selectable groups" setting. Once it has a list of its own, only what you put in that list counts — this writes to the server immediately and is not part of the cell changes saved below.
qy_ugl_create_carries: The list is seeded with the **{{count}} model groups this tier can actually use right now**, unchanged, so nobody loses anything on this click; your add/remove is applied on top of that.
qy_ugl_create_discards_draft: ⚠ You still have unsaved cell changes. Creating the list writes to the server and reloads the real state, which discards them — save or reset them first, then come back.
qy_ugl_scope_write_discards_draft: ⚠ You still have unsaved cell changes. This is a separate scope write; once it succeeds the real server state is reloaded and those changes are discarded — save or reset them first, then come back.
qy_ugl_create_confirm: Create the list and apply this change
qy_ugl_clear_title: Removing "{{modelGroup}}" leaves this tier with no model group at all
qy_ugl_clear_desc: "Nothing left" has two opposite meanings, and which one "{{userGroup}}" should get is your call. There is no default action here.
qy_ugl_clear_fallback: Fall back to the global list (usually what you want)
qy_ugl_clear_fallback_desc: Delete this tier's own list so it follows the global "user selectable groups" setting again. That usually means this tier can use **more**, not that it is disabled. Ratios are kept as they are (ratios and the list are two separate records); per-cell notes survive only for entries that are still included when you rebuild the list — rebuilding seeds it from what the tier can actually use at that moment instead of quietly reviving today's list.
qy_ugl_clear_fallback_action: Delete the list, fall back to global
qy_ugl_clear_isolate_desc: Keep a list of its own but leave it empty. Under "enforce now", tokens from this tier that name a model group explicitly get a 403; tokens with an empty group skip the check entirely and keep working — an empty list does not stop those.
qy_ugl_mode_enforce_desc: Model groups outside the list cannot be selected by this tier's keys, and such requests get a 403.
qy_ugl_mode_enforce_intro: After the switch, model groups outside the list really are blocked: this tier's tokens pointing at them get a 403 immediately. It is the only action on this page that cuts a batch of users off at once, so look at the impact report first.
qy_ugl_advanced: More scope settings (auto pseudo-group / note on this list)
qy_restricted_banner_title: Your account is restricted — support tickets are the only thing still available
qy_restricted_blocked: Unavailable while restricted: API calls (existing keys are rejected with a 403 too), creating or editing keys, balance transfers, commission withdrawals, top-ups and redemption codes, check-in, lottery and betting, subscription purchases, profile and password changes, and every admin function.
qy_restricted_kept: Your quota, usage logs, keys, tickets and violation records are all kept as they are and come back the moment the restriction is lifted — nothing has to be set up again.
qy_restricted_appeal_hint: To appeal, open a ticket and explain the situation. Once an administrator lifts the restriction, sign in again and everything works as before.
qy_restricted_no_channel: Tickets are not enabled on this site. Please reach an administrator through the contact details in the site announcement.
qy_restricted_landing_title: This page is unavailable while your account is restricted
qy_restricted_landing_desc: You are still signed in, but access is narrowed down to the pages you need in order to appeal.
qy_plaza_anon_preview_notice: Guest preview: the models and prices below are those of the group new accounts start in. Sign in to see the ones for your own group.
qy_plaza_anon_empty_title: No models available for the default group
qy_plaza_anon_empty_desc: The group new accounts start in currently has no usable model groups, so there is nothing to show. Sign in to see the models available to your own group.
qy_vio_batch_select_all: Select every rule on this page
qy_vio_batch_enable_desc: {{total}} rule(s) selected; {{count}} of them are currently disabled and will actually be turned on. The rest are already enabled and will not change.
qy_vio_batch_disable_desc: {{total}} rule(s) selected; {{count}} of them are currently enabled and will be turned off. Disabling a protection rule raises no error and shows no warning anywhere - the only symptom is that it will never match again.
qy_vio_batch_enforce_title: {{count}} of them are in enforce mode
qy_vio_batch_enforce_desc: They start charging, blocking and counting toward auto-ban the moment they are enabled. Shadow rules only record. This bulk action never changes any rule's shadow/enforce mode - that can only be done when editing a single rule.
qy_vio_batch_scope_desc: Set the group scope of the {{count}} selected rule(s). "Group" here means the model group - matching compares the group this request was actually routed to, not which tier the user belongs to.
qy_vio_batch_scope_op: What to do with the existing list
qy_vio_batch_op_append_desc: Add the groups you type to the end of each rule's existing list, skipping ones already there. No existing group is lost.
qy_vio_batch_op_replace_desc: Swap each rule's whole list for the groups you type, discarding every existing entry, and rewrite the direction to the one selected below. Leave it empty to clear the scope.
qy_vio_batch_op_remove_desc: Take the groups you type out of each rule's existing list and leave the rest alone. A rule whose list ends up empty applies to every group.
qy_vio_batch_scope_mode_desc: The same list of names means opposite things in the two directions: "Only these groups" applies the rule solely to the listed groups; "All except these groups" exempts them and applies to everything else. That is why this field is required and has no default.
qy_vio_batch_scope_mode_mismatch_hint: Append and remove never flip a rule's direction for you. Rules whose direction differs from the one selected above are left untouched and listed separately in the result. Use "Replace" if you want to unify the direction.
qy_vio_batch_scope_clear_desc: "Replace" with no groups means these {{count}} rule(s) will apply to every model group on the site from now on. That widens their reach, it does not narrow it.
qy_vio_batch_scope_confirm_append: {{groups}} will be appended to the group scope of {{count}} rule(s) (direction: {{mode}}). Existing groups are kept; rules whose direction differs are skipped.
qy_vio_batch_scope_confirm_replace: The group scope of {{count}} rule(s) will be replaced with {{groups}} (direction: {{mode}}). Every existing group name on those rules is discarded and cannot be restored from the UI.
qy_vio_batch_scope_confirm_remove: {{groups}} will be removed from the group scope of {{count}} rule(s) (direction: {{mode}}). Rules left with an empty list apply to every group; rules whose direction differs are skipped.
qy_vio_batch_report_summary: {{total}} total: {{done}} changed, {{skipped}} needed no change, {{failed}} did not go through.
qy_vio_batch_toast_nothing: All {{count}} selected rule(s) were already in this state - nothing changed
qy_vio_batch_toast_failed: {{count}} rule(s) did not go through - see the details
qy_vio_batch_item_not_found: Rule not found; another admin may have deleted it. Refresh the list.
qy_vio_batch_item_no_change: Already in the target state, nothing to do
qy_vio_batch_item_wont_compile: This rule does not compile; enabling it would never match anything. Fix its pattern first.
qy_vio_batch_item_scope_too_long: The resulting group list would exceed the length limit, so this rule was left unchanged
qy_vio_batch_item_direction_mismatch: This rule's list direction differs from the one you chose. Append/remove will not flip it for you - run two batches or use "Replace".
qy_vio_batch_item_enforce_ack: This rule was just switched to enforce mode and was not covered by this confirmation. Refresh the list and confirm again.
qy_vio_batch_item_stale: Another admin just changed this rule, so it was not overwritten. Refresh the list and retry.
qy_vio_batch_item_db_error: Write failed; check the backend logs
qy_vio_field_status_scope_desc: Upstream HTTP status precondition. Empty = any; accepts 400, 400,403 or 400-499. It is ANDed with the match type, so status code plus error body can be a single rule; split across two rules, one upstream refusal would be counted and charged twice.
qy_vio_err_status_scope_phase: Status code scope only applies to upstream phases: before forwarding there is no upstream response, so the status is always 0 and the rule would never match.
qy_vio_policy_intro_title: Per user group: how many hits, over what window, and what happens then.
qy_vio_policy_intro_fallback: User groups without a dedicated policy fall back to the default tier. The default tier cannot be deleted - removing it would leave those groups pointing at a policy that does not exist.
qy_vio_policy_intro_disabled: Disabling a tier means that group falls back to the default tier, not that the group becomes exempt.
qy_vio_policy_intro_actions: Restrict and Ban set the same account status (restricted: can sign in, can only open tickets, everything else returns 403). The only difference is that Ban also revokes every login session.
qy_vio_policy_two_lines_note: There are two independent lines; crossing either one triggers action. (1) The account-wide line is the threshold you configure per user group on this page; it spans all violation categories. (2) The per-category line is each category's own threshold, configured on the Violation Categories page. What happens after crossing (record only / restrict / ban) is decided here, but "how many times" has two sources - a category line may take a user out before the number on this page does.
qy_vio_policy_fallback_from_yaml: The current fallback values come from YAML, not from a row in this table. Nothing changed here affects groups without a dedicated policy until a default tier is saved.
qy_vio_policy_deleted: Policy deleted; that group now falls back to the default tier
qy_vio_policy_action_record_desc: Crossing the threshold only leaves a row in the ban list. The account is untouched. Use this to observe before tightening.
qy_vio_policy_action_restrict_desc: Sets the account to restricted: can sign in, can only open tickets, all API calls return 403. The console session is kept so the user sees it immediately and can appeal.
qy_vio_policy_action_ban_desc: Same as Restrict, plus revoking every login session. The account status is identical; that extra step is the only difference.
qy_vio_policy_edit_desc: This tier applies only to the user group entered here; every other group still uses the default tier.
qy_vio_policy_edit_default_desc: Every user group without a dedicated policy is judged by this tier. It cannot be deleted and has no disable switch - there is no lower tier to fall back to.
qy_vio_policy_field_group_desc: Group names are case-insensitive. Entering a name that does not exist is not an error, but the tier will never take effect (that group silently falls back to the default tier).
qy_vio_policy_field_threshold_desc: Hits accumulated within the window that trigger the action. 0 means this tier takes no automatic action.
qy_vio_policy_field_enabled_desc: When off, the group falls back to the default tier - it does not become exempt.
qy_vio_policy_impact_title: Impact: accounts already past this line once saved
qy_vio_policy_impact_threshold_off: Threshold is 0, so this tier takes no automatic action. Impact is 0.
qy_vio_policy_impact_failed: Could not evaluate how many accounts this change would push past the line. If this is a tightening, confirm with care.
qy_vio_policy_impact_count: {{count}} account(s) are already past this line. Saving does not act on anyone; each of them is handled as {{action}} on their next violation hit.
qy_vio_policy_impact_capped: Scan limit reached; the real number may be higher.
qy_vio_policy_impact_all_groups: The default tier is estimated across all groups (it matches every group without a dedicated policy, which is not a set that can be queried exactly), so this number is an overestimate.
qy_vio_policy_confirm_warning: Confirm once more: after saving, {{count}} account(s) already past the line will be handled as {{action}} on their next violation hit (saving itself acts on no one; no new rows appear in the ban list). This change is written to the audit log.
qy_vio_policy_saved_with_impact: Policy saved; {{count}} account(s) past the line will be handled by the new policy on their next violation hit
qy_vcat_two_lines_note: There are two independent lines; crossing either one triggers action. (1) The account-wide line spans all categories and is configured per user group under Violation Enforcement Policy. (2) The per-category line is the threshold on this page. What happens after crossing (record only / restrict / ban) is always decided by the group policy of the user - this page only decides how many times.
qy_vcat_form_desc: A category is the bucket violations are counted into: hits from every rule bound to it accumulate on the same counter.
qy_vcat_sec_public_warning: These two fields are shown to users verbatim. Do not copy the internal notes here - those describe the matching criteria, and publishing them tells users how to evade detection.
qy_vcat_sec_threshold_desc: Reaching this many hits within the window triggers enforcement. 0 means this category has no line of its own; its hits still count toward the account-wide line. The action (record / restrict / ban) is configured per user group under Violation Enforcement Policy, not here.
qy_vcat_field_key_desc: Lowercase letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. External review sources (such as AI review) bind to this key; changing it breaks existing bindings.
qy_vcat_field_key_fallback: Uncategorized is the fallback category; its key cannot be changed because every rule without an explicit category lands here.
qy_vcat_field_name_desc: For operators only; may contain internal code names. Never shown to users.
qy_vcat_field_remark_desc: Matching criteria and typical false positives. Admin only.
qy_vcat_field_threshold_desc: 0 = this category does not trigger enforcement on its own.
qy_vcat_err_key_charset: Key may only contain lowercase letters, digits, underscore and hyphen
qy_vcat_err_public_title_required: A public title is required when the category is shown to users (the internal name is not a substitute)
qy_vcat_err_window_range: Window must be at least 1 hour; use "No time limit" if you do not want it to reset on time
qy_vcat_confirm_desc: {{count}} account(s) already exceed the new threshold for this category. Saving does not act on anyone; they will be handled on their own next violation according to their group policy.
qy_vcat_archive_desc: The {{count}} rule(s) in this category will be reassigned to Uncategorized, and no new violation records will land in this category.
qy_vcat_archive_records_note: Archiving is not deletion: existing violation records, evidence and this category historical counters are all kept - they are the basis for appeal review and ban post-mortems. The same key can be created again afterwards.
qy_vio_cat_desc: These are the violation categories this site counts, and your current count in each.
qy_vio_cat_account_line: Account total (all categories): {{hit}} / {{threshold}} within {{hours}}h; at {{threshold}} you will be {{action}}.
qy_vio_cat_account_line_off: Account total (all categories): {{hit}} within {{hours}}h; no overall threshold is set
qy_vio_cat_any_line_note: The account total and each individual category are independent thresholds; reaching either one triggers enforcement.
qy_vcat_threshold_disabled: Set to {{count}} within {{hours}}h, but the threshold switch is off and it is not in effect
qy_vcat_unset_banner: {{count}} categor(ies) still have no threshold. Their hits are still counted and still feed the account-wide line, but they never trigger enforcement on their own - so "how many times in this category means a ban" currently has no answer.
qy_vcat_sug_title: Apply suggested thresholds to built-in categories
qy_vcat_sug_desc: Suggested values follow how unambiguous the intent is and how large the false-positive surface is: categories normal usage never hits are set tight, while frequency-based ones and those relying on an upstream verdict are set loose. It only fills blanks - thresholds you set by hand are never overwritten.
qy_vcat_sug_impact: This writes thresholds to {{count}} categor(ies) that have none. Afterwards, based on existing counters, {{users}} account(s) are immediately over the line.
qy_vcat_sug_action_note: What happens after crossing is decided by the user's group enforcement policy; the current fallback policy is "{{action}}".
qy_vcat_sug_not_immediate: Applying does not act on anyone: it only writes the category table. Accounts already over the line are handled on their own next violation - no new rows appear in the ban list right after you click.
qy_vcat_sug_capped: The over-the-line account count hit the scan cap; the real number may be higher.
qy_vcat_sug_row_impact: {{count}} account(s) are already over this line.
qy_vcat_sug_applied: Thresholds written for {{count}} categor(ies); {{users}} account(s) are currently over the line and will be handled on their own next violation.
qy_vio_cat_sentence: You have violated [{{title}}] {{hit}} time(s); at {{threshold}} you will be {{action}} (counted within {{hours}}h).
qy_vio_cat_sentence_off: You have violated [{{title}}] {{hit}} time(s). This category is recorded only and has no ban threshold.
qy_vio_cat_remaining_none: Threshold reached; your next violation will be handled as "{{action}}".
qy_vio_cat_remaining_done: Threshold reached; this account has been handled as "{{action}}". If you believe this is wrong, you can appeal from the records below.
qy_vio_field_category_desc: Hits from this rule accumulate on the selected category counter. Hits from every rule in the same category add up; reaching that category threshold triggers enforcement. Leaving it unset lands the rule in Uncategorized, whose threshold defaults to 0 (no separate trigger).
qy_ai_settings_desc: Randomly sample a share of requests and send them to an external model for content review. What counts as a violation and what happens on a hit are still configured under Violation Rules — AI is simply one more match type (ai_review).
qy_ai_third_party_title: Sampled request content is sent to a third party
qy_ai_third_party_desc: Once enabled, the body of sampled user requests is sent to the review endpoint configured below. Confirm this is consistent with your privacy policy and terms of service first.
qy_ai_third_party_ack: I confirm that user request content will be sent to a third-party review service
qy_ai_not_effective_desc: The master switch, the scope policies (none at all — or every one of them with both sampling rates at 0 — counts as off), a usable channel (currently {{channels}}), and at least one ai_review rule: miss any of the four and no review call is ever made.
qy_ai_pre_timeout_hint: ⚠️ Pre-forward review must be synchronous (a hit has to be able to block the request), so this value is added directly to the latency of sampled requests. Maximum {{max}} ms. A timeout always allows the request through.
qy_ai_async_timeout_hint: Post-forward review is asynchronous — it only records and counts, and never affects the current request, so it does not cost the user any time. Maximum {{max}} ms.
qy_ai_max_input_hint: Both a cost gate and a privacy gate: every character sent costs money and leaves this site. Longer input keeps the head and tail halves.
qy_ai_prompt_cat_missing_desc: These categories are missing from the prompt that is actually sent: {{names}}. The list is supposed to be spliced in automatically, so this warning means the splice step failed — usually the category table did not load this round. While it lasts the model will not return those categories and rules filtering on them will not fire. Reload the page; if it persists, check the server logs.
qy_ai_prompt_cat_missing_title: The category list was not spliced into the prompt
qy_ai_prompt_cat_unknown_desc: These names appear in the prompt but not in the category table: {{names}}. They are usually left over from a hand-copied list in an older version — the authoritative list is appended after it, but the model may still answer with an old name, and that verdict is folded into "uncategorized". Fix it by deleting the hand-copied line (the list is spliced in automatically) or by creating those names as real categories. Current values: {{known}}.
qy_ai_prompt_cat_unknown_title: The prompt lists categories that are not in the category table
qy_ai_prompt_hint: The review result must be structured JSON. The violation category list is generated automatically from the Violation categories page and spliced into the prompt before sending — there is nothing to keep in sync by hand here. Categories currently in review: {{categories}}. A rule's category filter must match these values exactly, or the rule never fires.
qy_ai_prompt_source_custom_desc: This site uses its own prompt. It will keep using exactly what you wrote — future upgrades to the built-in default (including hardening against prompt injection) will no longer reach this field. Use "Restore default" below to follow the built-in prompt again.
qy_ai_prompt_source_default_desc: This site uses the built-in default prompt (stored as empty), so it follows future upgrades automatically. The text above is the full default — edit it in place; changing a single character makes it "Customized" on save and decouples it from the default from then on.
qy_ai_failopen_title: Review failures always allow the request
qy_ai_failopen_desc: Timeouts, malformed JSON, 5xx responses, and every channel being unavailable all let the request proceed upstream unblocked. Every call, including failures, is recorded in the cost statistics below and can be filtered by outcome.
qy_ai_channels_desc: Add as many as you need; traffic is split randomly by weight and falls through to the next channel when one fails. The default endpoint and model name are pre-filled — supply your own key.
qy_ai_channels_empty: No review channel configured yet. With no usable channel, sampled requests are always allowed through.
qy_ai_key_missing_desc: violation.ai_review_key is empty in the server configuration, so channel keys cannot be saved (keys must be stored encrypted — this site never stores them in plaintext). Generate one with openssl rand -base64 32, add it to the config and restart. Self-hosted review services that need no authentication can leave the key empty.
qy_ai_f_base_url_hint: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, e.g. https://api.deepseek.com/v1. A URL ending in /chat/completions is also accepted.
qy_ai_f_api_key_hint_new: Leave empty if the service needs no authentication. Keys are stored encrypted; after saving only the last 4 characters are shown and no endpoint ever returns the plaintext.
qy_ai_f_api_key_hint_existing: A key is configured ({{hint}}). Leave this field untouched to keep it, enter a new key to replace it, or clear the field to remove it.
qy_ai_f_timeout_hint: 0 follows the global timeout. A local small model and a hosted large model differ by an order of magnitude, which is why this is per channel.
qy_ai_f_price_hint: Used to turn tokens into a cost figure. Leave at 0 if the price is unknown; cost for this channel then reads 0 and is flagged as price-not-configured.
qy_ai_cost_desc: AI review costs money. This covers tokens and spend for every call, including misses and failures.
qy_ai_unpriced_desc: {{count}} reviews have an unreliable cost: at least one channel they used has no price configured, so those attempts counted as 0. With failover a single review can hit up to three channels, and one unpriced channel makes the whole review a lower bound. The total above is less than what you actually spent.
qy_vio_field_ai_min_confidence_desc: 0..1, where 0 means no minimum. When the review model reports a violation but is less confident than this, the rule does not fire — it is the only false-positive gate AI review has. Put the categories to match in "Pattern" (comma separated; empty matches any violation).
qy_vio_err_ai_phase: AI review can only run pre-forward (synchronous, can block) or post-forward (asynchronous, record and count only)
qy_vio_err_async_match: Post-forward (async) supports AI review only: every other match type can be decided locally, and deferring it merely gives up the ability to block
qy_vio_err_async_action: Post-forward (async) supports "record only": the async stage has no billing context for this request, so a charge cannot be routed to the right quota pool
qy_vio_err_ai_confidence: Minimum confidence must be between 0 and 1 (0 means no minimum)
qy_vio_err_ai_confidence_type: Minimum confidence only applies to AI review; setting it on another match type has no effect
qy_cu_scope_hint: Covers every user who has a referral relationship or any commission activity. Amounts use the in-site balance format, the same number the user sees in their wallet.
qy_cu_empty_desc: Try another username / ID / email, or turn the filters off.
qy_cu_settled_hint: These are accrual rows already settled (status = settled). No admin endpoint exposes settlement documents today, so this tab answers "which money has landed in the balance" from the accrual ledger instead of inventing a settlement list.
qy_cu_block_default_reason: Stopped manually from the user commission page
qy_cu_rel_semantics: None of these actions touches commission already produced: accrued, settled, even already withdrawn amounts are all kept. They only change whether new commission is produced from now on. To take back paid commission, use Clawback instead.
qy_cu_rel_desc_set_inviter: This user has no inviter yet. Once set, their future top-ups and usage will pay commission to that inviter.
qy_cu_rel_desc_replace_inviter: Point this user at a different inviter. Future commission goes to the new one; everything already produced stays with the old one.
qy_cu_rel_desc_remove_inviter: Unbind this user from their inviter, so no new commission is produced for that inviter.
qy_cu_rel_desc_add_invitee: Make another user an invitee of this one. That user must not already have an inviter, otherwise the backend rejects it.
qy_cu_rel_target_hint: Enter the other user's ID. Self-invites and referral cycles of any length are rejected.
qy_cu_rel_reason_ph: Why this referral is being changed (at least 4 characters, written to the audit log)
qy_cu_rel_kept_from_inviter: Historical commission kept by the current inviter
qy_err_rel_same_inviter: That is already this user’s inviter, so there is nothing to change. Enter a different user ID to move them.
qy_cm_block_no_relation: This row is not attached to any referral relationship (manual adjustment rows belong to no invite pair), so commission cannot be stopped here. Nothing was changed.
qy_ai_prompt_preview_desc: The violation category list is generated from the Violation categories page and spliced into the prompt automatically, so the editor above is not everything the model reads. Add or remove categories on that page; to control where the list appears, put the {{placeholder}} token in your prompt.
qy_ai_prompt_preview_title: Preview: the prompt actually sent to the review model
qy_ai_scope_category_loading: The violation category list has not loaded yet, so only "Not specified" can be picked right now. Existing bindings are untouched; saving will not clear them.
qy_ai_scope_desc: Decide who gets reviewed, how much, and where it is sent, by user group and model. The table is in match order: a request takes the first policy that matches and stops there; if none match it is **not reviewed at all** — there is no fallback tier, a group that is not in this table is not reviewed.
qy_ai_scope_f_async_hint: Post-relay review is asynchronous — it only records and counts, and costs the user no time — so it can run far higher than the pre-relay rate. 0 disables post-relay review for this tier.
qy_ai_scope_f_category_hint: Every hit under this policy is recorded under this violation category (overriding the one bound on the rule), and the per-category counter follows it. The category returned by the review model still only decides whether a rule matches, and is kept verbatim in the review log. "Not specified" keeps the rule's own category, exactly as before this field existed.
qy_ai_scope_f_groups_hint: Comma separated, *required*: a policy must be bound to specific groups and cannot match the whole site by being left empty. Matches the group the request actually used, case-insensitively; accounts with an empty group are treated as default.
qy_ai_scope_f_mode_hint: Include = applies only to the listed groups. Exclude (= every group outside the list) is no longer accepted on an enabled policy: it is equivalent to matching the whole site, and newly created groups fall into it automatically. To exempt a few groups, give them their own higher-priority policy with both sampling rates at 0.
qy_ai_scope_f_models_hint: Comma separated; empty means all models. Prefix and suffix wildcards are supported, e.g. gpt-4* and *-vision. Combined with groups using AND.
qy_ai_scope_f_pre_hint: ⚠️ Pre-relay review is synchronous: a sampled request waits for the verdict before it goes upstream, so this share decides how many requests carry that latency. 0 disables pre-relay review for this tier.
qy_ai_scope_f_priority_hint: Ascending: lower matches first. A request is sampled by the first matching policy only; policies do not stack.
qy_ai_scope_f_prompt_hint: This only replaces the judgement guidance. The violation category list is always generated from the category table and appended for you, so do not hand-copy a list here: if you do, categories you create later will never be returned for this policy. Use the {{placeholder}} placeholder to choose where the generated list goes.
qy_ai_scope_group_empty: This site has no groups defined yet. Typed names still work.
qy_ai_scope_group_failed: Could not load the group list. Typed names still work; spelling just is not checked this time.
qy_ai_scope_group_loading: Loading the site group list — you can type a name instead of waiting.
qy_ai_scope_group_pick: Pick a group defined on this site
qy_ai_scope_group_required: At least one user group must be bound. An empty list means "all groups" — this tier's sampling rate would then apply to every user on the site and send a share of their request content to a third-party review service, while looking exactly like a policy that watches a single group. Pick a group from the dropdown above, or type a group name directly (historical groups are accepted too).
qy_ai_scope_group_unknown: Not in the site group list: {{groups}}. Historical groups (removed from the ratio table but still on some accounts) are normal; otherwise this is most likely a typo — and a typo means this policy monitors nothing at all, with no error anywhere.
qy_ai_scope_group_unknown_hint: Not in the site group list
qy_ai_scope_mode_exclude_blocked: An enabled policy cannot use Exclude: it matches every group *outside* the list, which is the same thing as leaving the list empty — and it widens over time, since a group created tomorrow is monitored automatically without anyone configuring it. Use Include and list the groups to monitor. To exempt a few groups, give them their own higher-priority policy with both sampling rates at 0.
