qy_ai_scope_none_desc: Nothing is being monitored: either no policy exists yet, or every tier has both sampling rates at 0. No review call will be made (the global fallback sampling rate is gone — there is no hidden default behind this any more). To start monitoring, add a scope policy with a rate above 0 and enable it.
qy_ai_scope_none_title: No group is being monitored right now
qy_ai_scope_prompt_placeholder: Leave empty to use the global prompt from "Review settings" above. Only write one here when this policy judges by a different standard than the rest of the site.
qy_ai_scope_sep_desc: Fullwidth comma, ideographic comma and semicolons are not separators — only the ASCII comma and newlines are. Writing "vip,svip" makes it one group literally named "vip,svip", which matches nobody, and nothing reports an error.
qy_ai_scope_sep_title: The scope contains a character that is not a separator
qy_ai_scope_unbound_active: Legacy: no group bound, currently matching the *entire site*. New writes no longer accept this, but it was not disabled automatically (silently switching off a live control is worse). Edit it to add groups, or disable it.
qy_ai_scope_unbound_idle: Legacy: no group bound (empty list, or Exclude direction = every group outside the list). It cannot be enabled until groups are added.
qy_vcat_all_idle_banner: No category has a threshold right now — not even the Uncategorized fallback. Rules still match and still count, but the per-category line will never trigger enforcement. To make rules actually able to ban, set thresholds here, or configure the account-wide line under Violation Enforcement Policy.
qy_vcat_err_ai_guidance_len: The AI review guidance is too long (limit {{max}} characters). It is paid for as tokens on every review call — tighten the criteria rather than lengthening the text.
qy_vcat_err_key_reserved: The key "none" is reserved: AI review uses it to mean "no violation". Creating a category with that key makes the model's value list contradict itself. Pick a different key.
qy_vcat_field_ai_guidance_desc: Tell the review model what belongs in this category and what does not. Boundaries help more than length ("anything involving minors goes to the other category", "asking for help does not count"). Leave it empty and the model only sees the key and name, which costs accuracy. Limit is 256 characters — this text is paid for as tokens on every review call.
qy_vcat_field_ai_participates_desc: Turn this off to keep the category out of the list sent to the review model. Only categories whose evidence is not text belong off — distillation is judged by request rate, upstream refusal by the upstream 4xx. Listing them makes the model guess from a single request, and a wrong guess is counted against a category that means something else entirely.
qy_vcat_sec_ai_desc: This text is sent to your third-party review service along with the review prompt. It is a third, separate copy: the internal note is admin-only, the public description is shown to users and must never state detection criteria, and this one states exactly those criteria. Never copy one into another.
qy_vio_field_category_dest_active: Hits are counted against "{{name}}". Reaching {{count}} hits within {{hours}}h on that category triggers enforcement (whichever line is crossed first, this one or the account-wide line).
qy_vio_field_category_dest_fallback_idle: No category selected, so hits are counted against the "{{name}}" fallback bucket — and that bucket has no threshold yet, so it only accumulates and never triggers enforcement on its own. In other words this rule will not ban anyone as configured. Pick a category that has a threshold, or set one for the fallback bucket on the Violation Categories page.
qy_vio_field_category_dest_idle: Hits are counted against "{{name}}", but that category has no threshold yet — it only accumulates, it never triggers enforcement on its own. Set a threshold for it on the Violation Categories page to make it fire.
qy_vio_field_category_dest_unknown: The category list cannot be read right now (still loading, or the request failed), so the destination shown here may not be the final one. Saving still works: a rule with no category always lands in Uncategorized.
qy_vio_field_count_weight_math_active: One hit adds {{weight}} to "{{name}}". That category fires at {{threshold}} within {{hours}}h, so about {{hits}} hits reach the line ({{hits}} x {{weight}} >= {{threshold}}).
qy_vio_field_count_weight_math_idle: One hit adds {{weight}} to "{{name}}", but that category has no threshold yet — no amount of counting will trigger enforcement on the category line; only the account-wide line still uses this weight. Set a threshold for it on the Violation Categories page to make it fire.
qy_vio_field_count_weight_math_zero: Weight 0: a hit is handled by the action above only (record / charge / block still happen) and adds nothing to the category counter or the account-wide line — this rule can never push anyone toward a ban. Set it to 1 to make hits count.
qy_vio_field_count_weight_math_unknown: One hit adds {{weight}} to whichever category this rule belongs to. The category list cannot be read right now (still loading, or the request failed), so the hits-to-threshold estimate is unavailable. Saving is unaffected.
qy_ai_sample_rate_moved_desc: Whether a request is reviewed is now answered only by the scope policies below: if no policy matches, the request is not reviewed at all — there is no hidden global default any more. Your previous global value was migrated into a policy covering every group (named 「全局兜底抽样率（迁移）」); edit, disable or delete it as you see fit.
qy_ai_sample_rate_moved_title: The global sampling rate is gone
qy_ai_scope_channel_disabled: The pinned channel is disabled: this tier will hit "no usable channel" every time and let the request through. It will not switch to another channel.
qy_ai_scope_channel_missing: The pinned channel cannot be found (deleted, or the channel list failed to load): this tier will hit "no usable channel" every time and let the request through. It will not switch to another channel.
qy_ai_scope_channel_broken_failover: The pinned channel is disabled or missing, but this tier has failover on: reviews still happen, they just land on the weighted-random pool every time - the endpoint you pinned is never used. Either enable it again, or confirm that sending to the other channels in the pool is acceptable.
qy_ai_scope_f_failover: Fall back to the weighted-random pool when the pinned channel is unusable
qy_ai_scope_f_failover_off: Off: only ever call the channel pinned above. If it times out, returns 5xx, has an expired key or gets disabled, this tier skips the review and lets the request through - it never switches to another channel. This is the default, and it is the literal meaning of "send it only here".
qy_ai_scope_f_failover_on: On: try the pinned channel first, then fill in from the remaining enabled channels by weight, up to 3 channels in the chain - all sharing the same single timeout budget, so latency is not multiplied. The cost, stated plainly: reviewed content may then be sent to endpoints you did not pin. A normal "no violation" verdict, and request-level rejections such as 400/413, never trigger a retry.
qy_ai_scope_f_channel_hint: Leave empty to pick randomly by weight among all enabled channels (channels have no priority; weight is how you express primary vs backup). Once pinned, this tier only ever calls that channel: if it is disabled or deleted the tier stops reviewing entirely and never falls back — because "it may only go to this one" is usually the whole reason for pinning it.
qy_ai_scope_form_desc: This tier decides who gets reviewed (groups and models), how much is sampled, which prompt is used, which review channel it is sent to, and which violation category a hit is recorded under. A snapshot reload is needed before it takes effect.
qy_vcat_threshold_disabled_unlimited: Set to {{count}} with no time limit, but the threshold switch is off and it is not in effect
qy_vio_cat_account_line_off_unlimited: Account total (all categories): {{hit}} in total (never resets on time); no overall threshold is set
qy_vio_cat_account_line_unlimited: Account total (all categories): {{hit}} / {{threshold}} in total; at {{threshold}} you will be {{action}}. This line never resets on time.
qy_vio_cat_sentence_unlimited: You have violated [{{title}}] {{hit}} time(s); at {{threshold}} you will be {{action}} (counted continuously, never reset on time).
qy_vio_counter_desc_unlimited: The fallback policy is currently set to "no time limit": the count never resets on time, and {{threshold}} triggers an automatic ban. Shadow hits are no longer counted. Counts recorded before this upgrade may still include shadow hits — reset them one by one here when needed (audited).
qy_vio_field_category_dest_active_unlimi: Hits are counted against "{{name}}". Reaching {{count}} hits in total on that category triggers enforcement, and the count never resets on time (whichever line is crossed first, this one or the account-wide line).
qy_vio_field_count_weight_math_active_un: One hit adds {{weight}} to "{{name}}". That category fires at {{threshold}} in total and never resets on time, so about {{hits}} hits reach the line ({{hits}} x {{weight}} >= {{threshold}}).
qy_vio_my_window_hint_unlimited: Counted continuously, never reset on time
qy_vio_window_unlimited_hint: When on, the count no longer resets on time. It accumulates from when this counter row was created, or from the last time it was cleared (an admin counter reset, a ban lift with "clear counter" ticked, or revoking a violation record all roll it back). It reads the counter, not the record table, so evidence retention cleanup never lowers the number - but the details of those older hits are no longer visible in the admin console.
qy_vio_window_unlimited_switch: No time limit: trigger on the count alone, however far apart the hits are
qy_gs_token_default_desc: Configured per user group: when a user in that group opens the New API Key dialog, the group dropdown is pre-selected with the model group set here. This only affects the pre-selected value in the create dialog — it does not change existing keys, nor request-time behavior. If the configured group is not actually selectable by that user, they simply get no pre-selection and fall back to the previous default.
qy_smtp_accounts_desc: Configure multiple sender mailboxes and spread the volume across them, so a single mailbox does not send so much in one hour that recipients start classifying the whole batch as spam (SMTP still returns success, so this is invisible to the sender). The old single-account SMTP form was migrated into the first row below on upgrade and has been removed — this table is now the only place SMTP is configured.
qy_smtp_no_accounts: No sender accounts yet. The single-account settings above are used until you add one.
qy_smtp_dialog_desc: Leave the password blank to keep it unchanged. Leave the From address blank to use the account itself.
qy_smtp_token_keep_hint: Leave blank to keep the existing password
qy_smtp_field_sort_order: Order (rotation order in sequential mode, lowest first)
qy_redemption_product_type_hint: A code redeems exactly one product. This cannot be changed after the code is created.
qy_redemption_product_type_locked: The product type is fixed when the code is created. Create a new batch to sell something else.
qy_redemption_plan_hint: Redeeming grants the user one subscription to this plan. Plans marked "pure product" carry no balance and only change the user group.
qy_redemption_plan_empty: No enabled plans yet. Create one on the subscription plans page first.
qy_redemption_quota_positive: Quota must be greater than 0 for a balance redemption code
qy_redemption_redeemed_plan_with_group: Redeemed! Activated: {{plan}}, user group upgraded to {{group}}
